title: Linux Terminal on iPhone and iPad | Acode
description: Use Acode’s emulated Alpine Linux terminal on iPhone and iPad. Learn about package installation, project files, and iOS runtime limitations.
heroHeadline: A Linux terminal alongside your iOS editor
heroSubheadline: Run shell commands in an emulated Alpine Linux environment while keeping your source files and editor close at hand.
problemPoints: Use Acode’s emulated Alpine Linux terminal on iPhone and iPad. Learn about package installation, project files, and iOS runtime limitations.
solutionPoints: Acode for iPhone and iPad is currently marked Coming soon on the website. Check the home page for release availability.
featuresHeadline: Linux Terminal on iPhone and iPad

features.title: An emulated Linux environment
features.description: Acode runs Linux tools through emulation on iOS. Commands and package installation can take time, especially for intensive work.

features.title: Packages for your workflow
features.description: Alpine uses apk to manage packages. Install only the tools you need and check that they work with the emulated runtime.

features.title: Plan for app suspension
features.description: Keep Acode in the foreground for terminal work. iOS may suspend the app in the background; do not rely on long-running jobs continuing unattended.

setupSteps.title: Open Terminal
setupSteps.description: Open the terminal from Acode and let the initial environment setup finish.

setupSteps.title: Check available packages
setupSteps.description: Run apk update, then use apk search to find a package.

setupSteps.title: Start small
setupSteps.description: Try a simple command before a larger build. Use a remote machine for workloads that exceed the local runtime’s capabilities.

faqs.question: Is this a native iOS shell?
faqs.answer: It is an emulated Alpine Linux environment inside Acode, not an unrestricted shell for the iOS operating system.

faqs.question: Will every Linux tool work?
faqs.answer: No. Compatibility depends on the emulator and package requirements. Tools that depend on unsupported kernel features or runtime behavior may not work.

faqs.question: Can commands run indefinitely in the background?
faqs.answer: No. iOS controls the app’s background lifetime. Keep the app active and save your work before switching away.
